newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet okays 26 bln baht 97/98 budget cut.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet okays 26 bln baht 97/98 budget cut.

text.p: Bank of Thailand deputy governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said on Wednesday the cabinet has approved a 26 billion baht cut to the 1997/98 (October/September) fiscal budget.
The cut will bring spending down to 982 billion baht from the originally planned 1,008 billion baht, he said.
"The cabinet has approved the budget cut and the Bank of Thailand has come here to explain how (the) budget cut will impact the economy," he said during a break in the cabinet meeting.
Chaiyawat said the cut was expected to take gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 1997 to around six percent and the current account deficit to approximately six percent of GDP.
Last year GDP grew by 6.7 percent and the current account deficit was 8.2 percent of GDP.

Inflation this year was expected not to exceed 4.8 percent, compared to 5.8 percent in 1996, he added. The 1997/98 budget cut will affect economic growth in 1997 as the fiscal year here starts in October.
"However, the Bank of Thailand will release the exact revised economic forecast for 1997 by the end of this month. This is because we must take the budget cut into account," Chaiyawat told reporters.
"The fiscal policy will have (a) strong impact on the assessment of the economy," he said.
